run.question: We're running low on disk space. Can you check our application indexes (app-187-*) and identify which one is consuming the most storage? Please tell me the index name and approximately how much space it's using.

report.summary: Among the application indices matching app-187-*, the largest by store size is app-187-metrics-analytics: 518,440 bytes (about 506 KiB / 0.49 MiB) with 5,000 documents, health green. Every other app-187-* index is tiny: the 20 app-187-logs-NN indices hold 10 documents each and 9,275 bytes each, except app-187-logs-10 at 9,375 bytes; the whole app-187-* set sums to roughly 704 KB (well under 1 MiB). The same 21 indices came back for an unfiltered "*" listing at query time, so no other index was present in this cluster then. This does not explain a low-disk condition on the queried cluster: the single node's Elasticsearch data filesystem (/usr/share/elasticsearch/data, overlay) reported 160.5 GB total, 96.9 GB available and 103.9 GB free, i.e. about 56.6 GB in use, at the same moment (query time, not the incident window). The cluster is yellow with 20 unassigned shards (24 active shards, 54.5% active), consistent with replica copies that cannot be allocated on a one-node cluster; the log indices carry health yellow for that reason while app-187-metrics-analytics is green. No fault root cause is asserted: this question is an inventory question and the storage figures do not support any index as a cause of a disk problem.

claims.text: app-187-metrics-analytics is the largest index among app-187-*: store.size 518,440 bytes (pri.store.size identical), 5,000 documents, status open, health green.

The remaining 20 indices matching app-187-* are app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20, each with 10 documents, each 9,275 bytes except app-187-logs-10 at 9,375 bytes; their sum plus app-187-metrics-analytics is about 704 KB, so the full app-187-* set occupies well under 1 MiB.

An unfiltered index listing (pattern "*") returned exactly the same 21 app-187-* indices (21 returned, 0 omitted, truncated false) at query time, so no additional index existed in this cluster at that moment.
Cluster health at query time was yellow: 1 node, 24 active shards, 24 active primary shards, 20 unassigned shards, 0 initializing, active_shards_percent_as_number 54.55.

The single node's Elasticsearch data filesystem (mount "/(overlay)", path /usr/share/elasticsearch/data) reported total_in_bytes 160,497,381,376 with free_in_bytes 103,880,241,152 and available_in_bytes 96,946,950,144 at query time — about 56.6 GB used and ~97 GB available — so this cluster's own disk reading does not corroborate a near-full disk, and the sub-1 MiB app-187-* indices cannot account for the used space.

The 20 yellow app-187-logs-* indices are yellow because their replica shards are the 20 unassigned shards reported by cluster health, which cannot be allocated on the cluster's single data node; this is a hypothesis about allocation, not an observed allocation failure message.

If disk pressure is real, look outside app-187-*: the app-187-* indices total under 1 MiB, so identify what else occupies the ~56.6 GB used on the /usr/share/elasticsearch/data overlay filesystem (other index data, shard copies, translog, or non-Elasticsearch files on the same mount) before deleting application indices.

gaps: elasticsearch_list_indices has no time range: the store sizes and document counts are the state at query time (observed_at 2026-11-23T17:39:06Z), so index storage during the authorized incident window 2026-10-24T17:39:03Z–2026-11-23T17:39:03Z is unknown.
Store sizes are only resolvable in byte units; with bytes=gb and bytes=mb every index rounded to "0", so size comparisons depend on the bytes=b reading (20 of 21 indices share the value 9,275).

The disk question's size ordering covers only indices matching app-187-*; nothing was read that enumerates what occupies the remaining ~56.6 GB on the data filesystem (shard data of other namespaces, snapshots, translog, or non-Elasticsearch data on the same overlay mount).
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change or retention-policy record can be checked to explain index growth or the low-disk report.
The origin of the human report of low disk space (alert, host, or volume other than this Elasticsearch node) was not identified, so which filesystem or volume is actually short is unknown.
next_steps: Inspect per-index store sizes and shard/segment breakdown for any indices outside app-187-* on the same data path, and check whether the low-disk report refers to a different host or volume.
Review disk watermark levels (low/high/flood_stage) on the node and the retention/ILM policy for app-187-logs-* if log volume is expected to grow.
Decide whether replica shards on app-187-logs-* are intended on this single-node cluster, since they cannot be allocated and keep the cluster yellow.
